description: Per-agent output schemas under the CANONICAL INTER-AGENT ENVELOPE (INFRA-037). Every agent emits ONE wrapper as body.payload: {"agent": str, "doc_id": str, "items": [ flat item, ... ]}. items is ALWAYS a list (singleton -> one element; nothing to report -> []). Each item is STRICTLY FLAT: values are scalars or arrays of scalars only -- no nested objects, no arrays of objects (structure is expressed as MORE items). Per-item CORE fields are enforced globally by AgentWrapper, not repeated per contract: model-owned ref, kind, confidence (CONFIDENT|UNCERTAIN), optional verdict, and ref_ids (flat citation array); runtime-owned item_id, revision, ts (stamped by make_envelope). The `fields`/`required` below are this agent's per-item AGENT-SPECIFIC flat fields. Convention-review agents must carry ref_ids (Part XVIII Section B). ref_ids may also carry WEB-REF-* ids (search-discovered web references minted from the structured web-source fields, INFRA-042), cited exactly like a REF-*.
envelope: canonical/v1 (INFRA-037): {agent, doc_id, items:[flat items]}; core per item = item_id(runtime), revision(runtime), ts(runtime), ref, kind, confidence, verdict(optional), ref_ids

finding_record.description: The typed inter-agent Finding record. Agents do not communicate with each other in natural language: a finding is stated in fields, and the sentence written for a person travels as `explanation`, which no other agent reads. One canonical-envelope item, so strictly flat: a measured quantity is a number field plus a unit-string field, never a nested object. The record's verdict lives in `record_verdict`, not in `verdict`: every agent already has a `verdict` field with its own declared values, and the verifiability gate fires on exactly those values, so the record must not overwrite them.

says.rule_id: the CONV-* id of the rule this finding applies, exactly as it appears in the convention registry you were given
says.source_rule_id: the operator's own id for that same rule when the registry entry carries one, so the finding can be attributed to the rule as it was written
says.unit_id: copy this EXACTLY from your work payload's document_units list (the unit_id field of whichever entry this finding is about, matched by its title). Never invent your own identifier for the unit (not its own name, its own label, or any value written inside it): a downstream lookup joins on this string against the pipeline's own unit ids, and any other string silently fails that join. If document_units is absent from your payload, leave unit_id empty rather than writing your own id for it.
says.value_a: the figure the document states, as a number with no separators
says.unit_a: the unit of value_a, as a short string
says.value_b: the figure it is compared against, as a number: a stated total, a band bound, or the same field's figure in the earlier version of the document
says.relation: what kind of comparison this is, one of the declared relations: a disagreement between two figures of this document, or (changed_from_prior, unchanged_from_prior, moved_toward, moved_away, absent_since_prior) a comparison of a field with the same field in an operator-declared earlier version of the document
says.record_verdict: ok when the unit satisfies the rule, irregular when it does not. This is the record's OWN verdict field and is separate from your agent verdict: keep setting `verdict` from your own contract's list as well. A comparison with the earlier version is always ok: movement is information, not an irregularity
says.source_refs: the REF-* or WEB-REF-* ids this finding rests on
says.explanation: one or two sentences for the person reading the review; no other agent reads this field
says.field_label: optional: the document's own label for the field value_a was read from, as words
says.delta: optional: value_a minus value_b, only when both carry the same unit
says.band_distance_change: optional: how far the field moved relative to the band the rule states, now minus the earlier version; negative is toward the band, positive away, zero unchanged; omit when no single band applies
says.provenance: optional: computed when the pipeline minted this record from figures it read itself; leave it unset when you write the record

fields.ref_ids: array of REF-* strings (required in convention review)
fields.finding_record: OPTIONAL, and the preferred shape when this finding is a comparison of two figures: set relation, verdict, rule_id, unit_id, value_a/unit_a, value_b/unit_b, source_refs, explanation. See the top-level finding_record block. Emit it as ordinary item fields, not as a nested object.

fields.source_url: string | null (a URL here mints a WEB-REF-* added to ref_ids, INFRA-042)
fields.ref_ids: array of REF-* strings (required in convention review)
fields.finding_record: OPTIONAL, and the preferred shape when this finding is a comparison of two figures: set relation, verdict, rule_id, unit_id, value_a/unit_a, value_b/unit_b, source_refs, explanation. See the top-level finding_record block. Emit it as ordinary item fields, not as a nested object.

fields.procedure_id: string. THE ONE name for the rule this item is about: the CONV-* id, exactly as it appears in the convention registry you were given. Do not also set conv_id or finding_record's own rule_id field for this: they do not exist as separate fields, procedure_id is read as both by every consumer.
fields.verdict: ALIGNED | ANTI_PATTERN | OUTDATED | NO_REFERENCE_AVAILABLE | COMPLIANT | VIOLATION | AMBIGUOUS
fields.reference_source: string | null (a URL or named source here mints a WEB-REF-*, INFRA-042)
fields.reference_url: string | null (a URL here mints a WEB-REF-*, INFRA-042)
fields.ref_ids: array of REF-* strings (required in convention review)
fields.relation: REQUIRED, not optional: what kind of comparison or defect this finding states. One of the declared relations (see the top-level finding_record block), e.g. missing_field, type_mismatch, sum_mismatch. This is not a second copy of verdict: verdict says ALIGNED/VIOLATION/etc, relation says WHAT KIND of thing you found.
fields.record_verdict: REQUIRED, not optional: "ok" or "irregular". This is the finding record's OWN verdict field, separate from your verdict field above (keep setting both; they are not the same field under two names). Set record_verdict="irregular" exactly when your own verdict names a problem (VIOLATION, ANTI_PATTERN, OUTDATED); set it "ok" when your verdict is COMPLIANT or ALIGNED.
fields.explanation: REQUIRED, not optional: one or two sentences, for the person reading the review, naming the SPECIFIC field, value, or passage that is wrong and why. "CONV-005 was violated" is not an explanation; "Type states 'Image', which is not one of Text/Sound/Dataset/Collection" is. A verdict with no explanation tells a reader nothing they can act on.
fields.field_label: optional: the document's own label for the field this finding is about, as words, e.g. "Rights" or "Creator". Always this name, never "field": no other name is read for this.
fields.finding_record:
The full shape this agent's own required relation/record_verdict/explanation above belong to (see the top-level finding_record block for every optional field beyond those three, e.g. unit_id, value_a/unit_a, value_b/unit_b). Emit every field as an ordinary item field, not as a nested object. The rule this compares against is procedure_id, above, already required: do not set a second rule_id field.

A FILLED EXAMPLE, the actual shape a real item takes, not a template: a record missing its Creator field looks like {"ref": "REF-0065", "kind": "finding", "confidence": "CONFIDENT", "procedure_id": "CONV-004", "verdict": "VIOLATION", "relation": "missing_field", "record_verdict": "irregular", "field_label": "Creator", "explanation": "Record CAT-ALDER has no Creator field, which CONV-004 requires for attribution.", "ref_ids": ["REF-0065"]}. Every one of relation, record_verdict and explanation is present, plainly, not left for a later pass to add.

directives: After reviewing what the document contains, consult the structural inventory in your context package (work_payload.structural_inventory). For any element present in more than half the corpus documents but absent from this operational document, emit an ADDITIONAL item with kind='absence', verdict='VIOLATION', ref='document-level', and ref_ids citing the corpus documents where the element appears. The recommendation should explain what structural element is missing and which corpus documents establish it as standard practice.

directives: After reviewing what the document contains, consult the structural inventory in your context package (work_payload.structural_inventory). For any legal mechanism (redress, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring, definitions, prohibitions, transparency obligations) present in more than half the corpus documents but absent from this operational document, emit an ADDITIONAL item with kind='absence', verdict='THIN' or 'UNSUPPORTED', explaining in the reasoning that the absence is the issue, and ref_ids citing the corpus documents where the mechanism appears.

ARCHIVIST.item_kind: index (per-document) or inventory (one item per corpus governance element)

fields.title: string | null
fields.element: string (inventory items: the governance element name)
fields.document_count: int (inventory items: how many corpus docs contain the element)
fields.document_names: array of strings (inventory items: which corpus docs)

directives: When work_payload.task == 'corpus_level_analysis', emit ONE item per governance element with kind='inventory': fields element, description, document_count, and document_names (a flat array of strings). Cover risk classification, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring, redress mechanisms, transparency obligations, human oversight, prohibited practices, environmental provisions, data flow provisions, definitions sections, and any other structural pattern seen in multiple documents. Indexing structural patterns across documents is indexing (within your DOES set), not analysis.

INST_FINDER.note: AUDIT-ONLY (intentional): this agent's corpus-level output is posted to the bus for auditability but is intentionally NOT consumed by any downstream agent or deliverable yet. This is by design, not a dropped handoff; it is a candidate input for future integration (e.g. an institution graph). Do not treat the missing downstream reader as a bug.

REDACTOR.item_kind: redaction (one item per proposed redaction; items:[] means nothing to redact)

fields.kind: redaction (REQUIRED value — every redaction item MUST set kind="redaction", never "finding")
fields.span: string (the exact text to redact, verbatim)
fields.rule_id: string (the id of the operator/default rule that matched this span, e.g. CONV-006 or RED-DFLT-001)

fields.context_refs: array of REF-* from the context corpus supporting the amendment
fields.finding_type: terminology | red_flag | rephrasing | citation_style | structural | borrowing | value_alignment | factual | procedural
fields.original_text: string — the exact text being amended
fields.proposed_text: string | null — proposed replacement (null if flag-only)
fields.comment: string, must contain >=1 CONV-* and >=1 REF-* (empty registry per INFRA-042: >=1 REF-* or >=1 WEB-REF-*, no CONV required)
fields.ref_ids: array of REF-* or WEB-REF-* strings (all citations; >=1 required)

location.says: a REF-* id such as REF-0001, copied from the reference index, or the exact sentinel 'document-level' when the finding is that something is absent and so has no anchor in the document

convention_ref.says: a single CONV-* id from the convention registry, such as CONV-007, and nothing else in the field

comment.says: prose that spells out at least one CONV-* id and at least one REF-* id inside the text itself, not only in the other fields
